INTRODUCTION
Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
(allo-HSCT) is the only curative treatment option for
‘myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) (1.2). However, itis often
difficult to find a well-matched donor for patients requiring
a transplant. To overcome this problem, HLA-haploidentical
related donor HSCT (haplo-HSCT) has become a valuable
option, Over the past 2 decades, there has been consider-
able progress in the field of haplo-HSCT, and an increasing
‘number of patients are benefiting from this technique (3.4).
Wang et al. [5] reported 4-year adjusted probabilities of
relapse and overall survival (OS) in haplo-HSCT of 6x to 7%
and 58% to 63%, respectively, which are comparable to values
for HLA-identical sibling donor (ISD) HSCT in patients with,
(MDS, suggesting that a haploidentical related donor may be
4 valid alternative when an ISD is not available.
Several prognostic tools, such as the standard Interna-
tonal Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS) [6], revised IPSS

(1PSs-R) [7], and World Health Organization Prognostic Scoring.
‘System (WPSS) [8], use disease-specific factors to deter-
mine the prognosis of patients with MDS. However, these
tools are not specific to patients undergoing transplanta-
tion and do not consider other factors that may contribute
to the decision to perform allo-HSCT. The Center for Inter-
national Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR)
has proposed a prognostic scoring system that includes 5
prognostic factors: age, percentage of peripheral blood blasts,
‘cytogenetic findings, performance status, and platelet count
[9]. The CIBMR score is highly prognostic of survival, disease-
free survival (DFS), treatment-related mortality, and relapse;
however, itis based on patients undergoing HSCT from ISDs
‘or well-matched unrelated donors (URDs). with haplo-
HSCT recipients excluded. Thus, the validity of the CIEMTR
prognostic scoring system in haplo-HSCT has not been
‘evaluated to date. In addition, there is no transplantation-
specific risk stratification too! for patients with MDS following
haplo-HSCT.
In this study, we evaluated the predictive ability of the
‘CIBMTR prognostic scoring system for patients with MDS fol-
lowing haplo-HSCT. In addition, here we propose and validate
a modified prognostic scoring system that may be more suit
able for haplo-HSCT recipients.
